newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu uses hard line to defend Arafat talks.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu uses hard line to defend Arafat talks.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu angered Palestinian negotiators by restating his opposition to a Palestinian state to defend his landmark meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

"You can dream every night...and you will still wake up every morning and see: There is no Palestinian state, there is no Palestinian state, there is not and there will not be a Palestinian state," Netanyahu told a meeting of his Likud bloc.

He began his speech to the hundreds-strong Likud central committee with a broadside at former prime minister Shimon Peres, whom he defeated in May elections, in which he also hailed Jewish settlement of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Palestinians say that settlement must stop but Netanyahu, who was loudly applauded, declared: "Jewish settlement in Judea and Samaria (the West Bank) will live, will thrive, will exist for ever."
One supporter of Netanyahu's decision to meet Arafat on Wednesday, Likud Tel Aviv Mayor Roni Milo, said the summit was necessary to honour deals reached by the previous government.
"We cannot...act like a state of cannibals and say we are not interested in what was, that there are agreements that don't interest us," said Milo, to boos from the audience.

Arafat economic adviser Khaled Salam slammed Netanyahu's speech. "Mr Netanyahu talks to us directly or through his envoys in one language and talks to the Israelis in another language completely," he told Reuters.

"His speech is making problems for the steering committee which will meet on Monday...We cannot in any case place Israeli- Palestinian relations and the whole political process hostage to political speeches such as Netanyahu's today."
Netanyahu and Arafat, meeting face-to-face for the first time, agreed to relaunch peace negotiations conducted through the steering committee.
Netanyahu, asked earlier on Israel television if he would dismiss ministers who did not fall into line with his policy, said: "If necessary, yes."

The two sides are still apparently far apart on all major issues relating to continuation of the 1993 framework peace deal reached by the previous Israeli government and the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
Netanyahu argues that there can be no expansion of Palestinian self-rule unless Israel's security needs are satisfied.

Palestinians want the implementation of peace deal clauses on an Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron and other areas of the West Bank and the opening of a passage for Palestinians to travel between the West Bank and Gaza.
